..
Confidence is increasing of a sustained trade-wind surge bringing 
breezy winds with near-gale gusts to the region by early next week, 
as a result of an increasing pressure gradient between the mid- 
latitudes and tropics. There is a chance of low-end scattered showers
and isolated thunderstorms tonight through tomorrow afternoon, 
before generally drier weather moves in associated with the building 
trade-winds. These winds will additionally make a fire weather watch 
and later a red flag warning likely Saturday morning, then Sunday 
morning. This is because they will be accompanied by a drop in 
dewpoints which will lower the afternoon relative humidities.

Marine...
The current trade-wind surge remains stronger than previously 
expected, with stronger winds found north near Saipan and Tinian. 
Guam and Rota will see frequent marginal Small Craft Advisory level 
gusts, while Tinian and Saipan waters will see sustained winds up to 
25 knots with frequent gusts to 30 knots. The winds could ebb for 12 
to 24 hours, then start to increase again Sunday. The winds on 
Sunday could be equal or even a bit higher than the winds from this 
last surge, with occasional gusts to gale strength likely. Seas will
also build, likely reaching 9 to 11 feet Monday through Wednesday.

Eastern Micronesia...
An active Near-Equatorial Trough is producing scattered to numerous
showers and isolated thunderstorms over portions of eastern
Micronesia. Showers look to slowly increase from scattered over
Kosrae tonight to numerous Saturday morning through afternoon. For
Pohnpei, scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms look to move
into the waters before midnight tonight, also becoming numerous
Saturday morning. Overall, a wetter pattern looks to continue for
Pohnpei through the middle of next week and for Kosrae through the
beginning of next week. 1 to 2 inches of rainfall are possible for
both locations over the next few days. For Majuro, a dry trade-wind
pattern will continue through the middle of next week. 

A trade-wind surge continues across Majuro, with fresh to strong
winds expected over the next few days. A building trade-wind swell is
also expected to move into the waters overnight. Therefore, a Small
Craft Advisory was issued for Majuro through early Thursday morning.
For Pohnpei, moderate to fresh winds are expected through the middle
of next week, with occasional strong gusts becoming frequent by
Sunday night. Seas are expected to build to around 10 feet by 
Sunday. For Kosrae, gentle to moderate winds with fresh gusts are
expected through the weekend, becoming moderate to fresh early next
week. Therefore, headlines were added to both forecasts for the
potential for a Small Craft Advisory beginning Sunday.

Western Micronesia...
Visible satellite imagery reveals partly cloudy skies with isolated 
showers at Palau and Yap, and mostly cloudy skies with scattered 
showers moving in from the northeast at Chuuk. Combined seas are
between 4 to 6 feet at all forecast locations.

A wetter pattern is in store for western Micronesia this weekend. A
few transient trade-wind troughs will move across Palau through
Sunday night--one of which will bring scattered showers around 
midnight tonight. As for Yap and Chuuk, an elongated portion of the 
Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) extending from eastern Micronesia will
bringing scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms for much of the
forecast period, eventually moving south over Palau next week. Some 
periods of numerous showers are likely this weekend for Chuuk. As for
the next work week, model guidance has trended the heaviest rainfall
more south of the region, so showers top out at 50 percent for Chuuk
and Palau and 40 percent for Yap. Considering the early onset of 
drought that began earlier this month, residents are urged to 
conserve and fill water reserves with the upcoming rainfall.

Fairly benign marine conditions are expected to slowly deteriorate 
this weekend. Light to gentle easterlies prevail at Palau and Yap, 
and gentle to moderate easterlies at Chuuk. A trade-wind surge will 
approach Chuuk earlier than previously expected with scatterometry 
showing 15 to 20 knot trade winds just northeast of Weno. Model 
guidance indicates gusts up to 25 knots beginning Saturday morning, 
so a Small Craft Advisory is issued and will be in effect starting 
at 5 AM ChST Saturday. This surge may also bring fresh to strong 
trade winds to Yap later this weekend, so a headline was included to
communicate the upcoming change in conditions. Early next week, an 
elevated trade swell may approach all forecast locations, bringing a 
potential east swell up to 8 feet at Chuuk and Yap. It is crucial 
that those with marine and surf interests monitor the forecast as 
these conditions could be hazardous to small craft and swimmers 
alike.
